I can talk smack on Overkill all day but I still play Payday 2 on my Xbox One (the console version doesn't have microtransations yet, so that might end up changing my mind when it updates).

The biggest issue I had with Overkill in the past is that they initially announced that Payday 2 would have equal support on the Xbox 360, whereas Payday 1 was PC/PS4 only. I bought the Xbox 360 version, but it never saw a single update to keep pace with the PC version. Overkill kept promising that it would, and that we just have to be patient, but eventually it fell off the radar again. Overkill blamed Microsoft's cap on update sizes, but even after that cap was removed, no updates came, even for bugs and core features that had been tweaked on PC.

Eventually the Xbox One came out, and rather than update the 360 version, Overkill decided to release the "Payday 2 Crimewave edition", which included all the updates available at that time on disc. I bought that one since I love the game and just wanted the updates. I was happy that it all came on disc, because I have a low bandwidth cap and can't download too much. Well the base game was buggier than the 360 version, and matchmaking literally did not work. That part didn't really matter to me because I only play with friends, but I understood everyone's frustration. Overkill promised a quick update to fix the issues, but it didn't come.

The console community felt slighted (again), so Overkill released a 9.8GB update. I was frustrated with the update because that's a quarter of my bandwidth cap (and the size of the game on disc, in fact), but I managed to get it downloaded with some rationing. To my surprise, the game still functioned identically to how it was before the update. Same bugs, same nonfunctional matchmaking. Other people complained, and it was discovered that the 9.8GB update was a complete placebo; it didn't fix anything. I suspect instead of fixing the issues, Overkill just had us redownload the whole game and pretended it was a bugfix update.

The game was finally updated with a much smaller bugfix update, but I don't suspect we'll get the same feature and level updates that the PC is already ahead on. That's fine with me because I also don't want the microtransation updates, but I think it illustrates my point about a good game that's hamstrung by bad devs. I'm happy with the game as it exists on Xbox One right now, but it sure was a lot of kicking and screaming to get to this point.
